records.source: וְדָרְיָ֨וֶשׁ֙ מָֽדָיָ֔אקַבֵּ֖ל מַלְכוּתָ֑א כְּבַ֥ר שְׁנִ֖ין שִׁתִּ֥ין וְתַרְתֵּֽין׃
records.gloss: And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about a son of years sixty and two.
pieces: And Darius the Mede took over the kingdom when he was about sixty-two years old.

L.1: And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about a son of sixty-two years.

R.1: Then Darius the Mede took over the kingdom. He was about sixty-two years old.

decisions.choice: This verse is 6:1 in the Aramaic text, 5:31 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: The Aramaic text begins chapter 6 with this verse. Many Bibles make it the last verse of chapter 5 (5:31), so their 6:1-28 is 6:2-29 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the text it translates. The verse joins the two stories: Belshazzar was killed (5:30), and Darius received the kingdom.

decisions.choice: Darius the Mede: a king not known outside Daniel
alternatives: a later memory of Darius I
decisions.reason: Daniel names Darius the Mede as the ruler who received Babylon after Belshazzar (also 9:1; 11:1), and the book places his reign before that of Cyrus the Persian (6:29). No Babylonian or Persian record names such a king; the records say that Cyrus himself took Babylon in 539 BC and ruled it, and the Darius who is well known, Darius I, reigned from 522 BC. Several identifications have been proposed: Gubaru (or Ugbaru), the general who took the city or the governor Cyrus set over Babylon; Cyrus himself, under another title (reading 6:29 as "in the reign of Darius, that is, the reign of Cyrus"); or a Median king Cyaxares, named by the Greek writer Xenophon. Others think that the book joins later memories of Darius I with the fall of Babylon. The text does not settle the question, and the translation gives the name as it stands.

decisions.choice: a son of sixty-two years: sixty-two years old
decisions.reason: "Son of so many years" is the Aramaic and Hebrew way of giving someone's age (Genesis 5:32).

decisions.choice: received (L); took over (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive, as a gift or an office. Literal keeps "received", which may hint that the kingdom was given to him (5:28; 9:1, "made king"); Balanced and Readable say "took over".

records.heading: Daniel and the officials of Darius

records.source: שְׁפַר֙ קֳדָ֣ם דָּרְיָ֔וֶשׁ וַהֲקִים֙ עַל־מַלְכוּתָ֔א לַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֖א מְאָ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֑ין דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֺ֖ן בְּכָל־מַלְכוּתָֽא׃
records.gloss: It seemed good before Darius, and he appointed over the kingdom satraps, a hundred and twenty, who would be in all the kingdom,
pieces: Darius decided to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,

L.2: It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom 120 satraps, who would be throughout the whole kingdom,

R.2: Darius decided to choose 120 regional governors to rule all the parts of his kingdom.

decisions.choice: This verse is 6:2 in the Aramaic text, 6:1 in Bibles that follow the Latin and later numbering
decisions.reason: Because the Aramaic text begins chapter 6 one verse earlier (see verse 1), each verse of this chapter is numbered one higher than in many Bibles: 6:2-29 here is their 6:1-28. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the text it translates.

decisions.choice: a hundred and twenty satraps: officials over the parts of the kingdom
decisions.reason: Under the Persian empire, a satrap governed one of its great regions, which numbered about twenty under Darius I. A hundred and twenty is far more, so here "satraps" may be used more loosely of governors of smaller districts; Esther speaks of 127 provinces (Esther 1:1). The officials of the conquered kingdom of Babylon may be meant.

decisions.choice: satraps (L, B); regional governors (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms for Daniel set. The number is written in figures at every level, since it is above ninety-nine. The sentence runs on into verse 3.

records.source: וְעֵ֤לָּא מִנְּהוֹן֙ סָרְכִ֣ין תְּלָתָ֔א דִּ֥י דָנִיֵּ֖אל חַֽד־מִנְּה֑וֹן דִּֽי־לֶהֱוֺ֞ן אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֗ין יָהֲבִ֤ין לְהוֹן֙ טַעְמָ֔א וּמַלְכָּ֖א לָֽא־לֶהֱוֵ֥א נָזִֽק׃
records.gloss: and above them overseers three, of whom Daniel [was] one of them, that these satraps would be giving to them account, and the king would not be suffering loss.
pieces: and over them three high officials, one of whom was Daniel. The satraps were to report to them, so that the king would not suffer loss.

L.3: and over them three overseers, of whom Daniel [was] one, so that these satraps might give account to them, and the king might not suffer loss.

R.3: Over these he put three leaders. Daniel was one of them. The regional governors had to report to these three leaders so that the king would not be cheated.

decisions.choice: overseers: high officials, chief ministers
decisions.reason: The word is borrowed from Persian and is used only in this chapter. It names the highest officers under the king, to whom the satraps reported.

decisions.choice: the king would not suffer loss: so that the king's revenues would be protected
decisions.reason: The overseers were to keep the satraps from cheating the king of taxes and tribute (compare Ezra 4:13, 15, 22, where the same word is used of harm to the king's interests).

decisions.choice: would not be cheated (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "suffer loss" means here (m2), and calls the satraps "regional governors".

records.source: אֱדַ֨יִן֙ דָּנִיֵּ֣אל דְּנָ֔ה הֲוָ֣א מִתְנַצַּ֔ח עַל־סָרְכַיָּ֖א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֑א כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֣י ר֤וּחַ יַתִּירָא֙ בֵּ֔הּ וּמַלְכָּ֣א עֲשִׁ֔ית לַהֲקָמוּתֵ֖הּ עַל־כָּל־מַלְכוּתָֽא׃
records.gloss: Then Daniel this was distinguishing himself above the overseers and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit [was] in him; and the king was planning to set him over all the kingdom.
pieces: Now Daniel distinguished himself above the other high officials and the satraps because of the extraordinary spirit in him, and the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

L.4: Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the overseers and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit [was] in him; and the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

R.4: Daniel did his work better than the other leaders and the regional governors, because he was unusually wise and able. So the king planned to put Daniel in charge of the whole kingdom.

decisions.choice: an extraordinary spirit: an exceptional mind and character
decisions.reason: The same words were used of Daniel in 5:12. The phrase covers both ability and character, as verse 5 shows: he was trustworthy.

decisions.choice: the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom: as Joseph over Egypt
decisions.reason: Like Joseph, the exile is raised to the second place in the realm (Genesis 41:40-43). The plan stirs the jealousy of the others.

decisions.choice: unusually wise and able (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "an extraordinary spirit" means here (m1).

records.source: אֱדַ֨יִן סָֽרְכַיָּ֜א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּ֗א הֲו֨וֹ בָעַ֧יִן עִלָּ֛ה לְהַשְׁכָּחָ֥ה לְדָנִיֵּ֖אל מִצַּ֣ד מַלְכוּתָ֑א וְכָל־עִלָּ֨ה וּשְׁחִיתָ֜ה לָא־יָכְלִ֣ין לְהַשְׁכָּחָ֗ה כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־מְהֵימַ֣ן ה֔וּא וְכָל־שָׁלוּ֙ וּשְׁחִיתָ֔ה לָ֥א הִשְׁתְּכַ֖חַת עֲלֽוֹהִי׃
records.gloss: Then the overseers and the satraps were seeking a pretext to find against Daniel from the side of the kingdom, and any pretext and corruption not were they able to find, because that trustworthy he [was], and any negligence and corruption not was found in him.
pieces: So the high officials and the satraps tried to find grounds for a charge against Daniel in his conduct of government affairs, but they could find no grounds and no corruption, because he was trustworthy; no negligence or corruption could be found in him.

L.5: Then the overseers and the satraps sought to find a pretext against Daniel in regard to the kingdom; but they could find no pretext or corruption, because he was faithful, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.

R.5: So the other leaders and the regional governors tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work. But they could not find anything wrong. He was honest and did his work well. He was never careless, and he never cheated.

decisions.choice: a pretext: a ground for accusation
decisions.reason: The word means a reason or occasion, here a charge that could be brought against Daniel.

decisions.choice: trustworthy: faithful, reliable
decisions.reason: The word is related to the Hebrew word for faithfulness and trust. In verse 24 Daniel is said to have trusted in his God, from the same root. His faithfulness to the king flows from his faithfulness to God.

decisions.choice: the way Daniel did his work (R)
decisions.reason: "From the side of the kingdom" means in his public duties; Readable says so in plain words.

records.source: אֱ֠דַיִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ אָֽמְרִ֔ין דִּ֣י לָ֧א נְהַשְׁכַּ֛ח לְדָנִיֵּ֥אל דְּנָ֖ה כָּל־עִלָּ֑א לָהֵ֕ן הַשְׁכַּ֥חְנָֽה עֲל֖וֹהִי בְּדָ֥ת אֱלָהֵֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: Then the men these were saying that not we will find against Daniel this any pretext unless we find [it] against him in the law of his God.
pieces: Then these men said, "We will never find any grounds for a charge against this Daniel unless it has to do with the law of his God."

L.6: Then these men said, "We will not find any pretext against this Daniel unless we find it against him in the law of his God."

R.6: Then these men said, "We will never find anything wrong with Daniel unless it has to do with the laws of his religion."

decisions.choice: the law of his God: the commands of Israel's God that Daniel kept
decisions.reason: The word for "law" is the one used for the king's decrees (2:9, 13, 15) and for "the law of the Medes and Persians" (verse 9). The story sets the two laws against each other. The only fault Daniel's enemies can find is his faithfulness to his God.

decisions.choice: this Daniel: with a touch of contempt
decisions.reason: "This Daniel" may carry a note of scorn, as of a foreigner.

decisions.choice: the laws of his religion (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the laws of his religion" for "the law of his God", which is what it means for these men.

records.source: אֱ֠דַיִן סָרְכַיָּ֤א וַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא֙ אִלֵּ֔ן הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ עַל־מַלְכָּ֑א וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לֵ֔הּ דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃
records.gloss: Then the overseers and the satraps these came thronging to the king, and thus saying to him: O Darius the king, forever live!
pieces: So these high officials and satraps went as a group to the king and said to him, "King Darius, may you live forever!

L.7: Then these overseers and satraps came thronging to the king and thus were saying to him, "O Darius the king, live forever!

R.7: So the leaders and the regional governors went together to the king. They said, "King Darius, may you live forever!

decisions.choice: came thronging: came as a group, perhaps in a plotting crowd
decisions.reason: The verb, used here and in verses 12 and 16, can mean to come in a crowd or in a rush, or to act together by agreement. It suggests a planned move by the whole group.

decisions.choice: King Darius, live forever: the greeting of the court
decisions.reason: As in 2:4.

decisions.choice: went as a group (B); went together (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of a crowd; Balanced and Readable give the sense (m1).

records.heading: The king's ban

records.source: אִתְיָעַ֜טוּ כֹּ֣ל׀סָרְכֵ֣י מַלְכוּתָ֗א סִגְנַיָּ֤א וַֽאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנַיָּא֙ הַדָּֽבְרַיָּ֣א וּפַחֲוָתָ֔א לְקַיָּמָ֤ה קְיָם֙ מַלְכָּ֔א וּלְתַקָּפָ֖ה אֱסָ֑ר דִּ֣י כָל־דִּֽי־יִבְעֵ֣ה בָ֠עוּ מִן־כָּל־אֱלָ֨הּ וֶֽאֱנָ֜שׁ עַד־יוֹמִ֣ין תְּלָתִ֗ין לָהֵן֙ מִנָּ֣ךְ מַלְכָּ֔א יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְגֹ֖ב אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃
records.gloss: Have taken counsel all the overseers of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, to establish a statute of [the] king and to make strong a prohibition, that any who asks a petition from any god or man for thirty days, except from you, O king, will be thrown into [the] den of the lions.
pieces: All the high officials of the kingdom, the prefects and satraps, the advisers and governors, have agreed that the king should issue a decree and enforce a ban: anyone who prays to any god or human being for the next thirty days, except to you, O king, will be thrown into the lions' den.

L.8: All the overseers of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have agreed together that the king should establish a statute and enforce a prohibition: that whoever makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the den of lions.

R.8: All the leaders of the kingdom, the prefects, the regional governors, the advisers and the governors have agreed that you should make a new law and make sure it is obeyed. The law will say that for thirty days no one may pray to any god or human being except to you, Your Majesty. Anyone who disobeys will be thrown into a pit of lions.

decisions.choice: all the overseers have agreed: a claim that was not true
decisions.reason: The plotters say that all the officials agree, but Daniel, one of the three overseers, was not asked. They mislead the king.

decisions.choice: petition to any god or man except the king: the king alone as the one to whom prayers are made
decisions.reason: The decree makes the king, for thirty days, the only one to whom requests may be made, whether to gods or people. Persian kings were not usually worshiped as gods, and the decree may be meant to show loyalty to the new ruler rather than to make him a god. Its real aim is to trap Daniel.

decisions.choice: the den of lions: a pit where lions were kept
decisions.reason: Assyrian and Persian kings kept lions for hunting and display. The "den" was probably a pit with an opening at the top that could be closed with a stone (verse 18).

decisions.choice: satraps (L, B); regional governors (R); the list kept
decisions.reason: The list of officials is kept at every level, with "regional governors" at Readable for the satraps. "Petition" means a prayer to a god or a request to a person, so Balanced and Readable say "pray to".

records.source: כְּעַ֣ן מַלְכָּ֔א תְּקִ֥ים אֱסָרָ֖א וְתִרְשֻׁ֣ם כְּתָבָ֑א דִּ֣י לָ֧א לְהַשְׁנָיָ֛ה כְּדָת־מָדַ֥י וּפָרַ֖ס דִּי־לָ֥א תֶעְדֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: Now, O king, establish the prohibition and sign the writing, that not [it is] to be changed, according to [the] law of [the] Medes and Persians, which does not pass away.
pieces: Now, O king, issue the ban and sign it in writing, so that it cannot be changed, as is the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."

L.9: Now, O king, establish the prohibition and sign the document, which is not to be changed, as a law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away."

R.9: Now, Your Majesty, make this law and sign it, so that it cannot be changed. This is the way the laws of the Medes and the Persians work. Once they are made, no one can cancel them."

decisions.choice: the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away: a law that could not be revoked
decisions.reason: Esther also says that a law written in the king's name and sealed with his ring could not be revoked (Esther 1:19; 8:8). The rule shows the king's authority, but here it traps the king himself (verses 15-16).

decisions.choice: This is the way the laws of the Medes and the Persians work (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the rule in two short sentences.

records.source: כָּל־קֳבֵ֖ל דְּנָ֑ה מַלְכָּא֙ דָּֽרְיָ֔וֶשׁ רְשַׁ֥ם כְּתָבָ֖א וֶאֱסָרָֽא׃
records.gloss: Because of this the king Darius signed the writing and the prohibition.
pieces: So King Darius signed the written ban.

L.10: Therefore King Darius signed the document, the prohibition.

R.10: So King Darius signed the new law.

decisions.choice: the document and the prohibition: the written decree
decisions.reason: The two words describe one thing: the written order that forbade petitions.

decisions.choice: the written ban (B); the new law (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two words into one (m1).

records.source: וְ֠דָנִיֵּאל כְּדִ֨י יְדַ֜ע דִּֽי־רְשִׁ֤ים כְּתָבָא֙ עַ֣ל לְבַיְתֵ֔הּ וְכַוִּ֨ין פְּתִיחָ֥ן לֵהּ֙ בְּעִלִּיתֵ֔הּ נֶ֖גֶד יְרוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְזִמְנִין֩ תְּלָתָ֨ה בְיוֹמָ֜א ה֣וּא׀בָּרֵ֣ךְ עַל־בִּרְכ֗וֹהִי וּמְצַלֵּ֤א וּמוֹדֵא֙ קֳדָ֣ם אֱלָהֵ֔הּ כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּֽי־הֲוָ֣א עָבֵ֔ד מִן־קַדְמַ֖ת דְּנָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And Daniel, when he knew that the writing was signed, went into his house, and windows [were] open to him in his upper room toward Jerusalem; and three times in the day he [was] kneeling on his knees and praying and giving thanks before his God, just as he had been doing before this.
pieces: When Daniel learned that the decree had been signed, he went home to his upstairs room, where the windows opened toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had always done.

L.11: And when Daniel knew that the document was signed, he went into his house, which had windows open in its upper room toward Jerusalem; and three times a day he knelt on his knees and prayed and gave thanks before his God, just as he had been doing before.

R.11: When Daniel heard that the new law had been signed, he went home. He went up to the room on the roof of his house. The windows of that room faced Jerusalem. Three times a day Daniel got down on his knees and prayed to God and thanked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, just as he had always done.

decisions.choice: windows open toward Jerusalem: prayer facing the place of God's temple
decisions.reason: Solomon prayed that God would hear his people when they prayed toward the land, the city and the temple from the land of their captivity (1 Kings 8:46-49). Daniel prays toward Jerusalem, though the temple lay in ruins.

decisions.choice: three times a day ... kneeling, praying, giving thanks
decisions.reason: Psalm 55:18 speaks of praying "evening and morning and at noon". Prayer at set times became the custom of Jews in exile. Daniel does not hide, and he does not change his practice; nor does he defy the king for show.

decisions.choice: just as he had been doing before: his habit of prayer
decisions.reason: The point is that he did not begin praying to provoke the king; he simply did not stop.

decisions.choice: upstairs room (B); the room on the roof (R)
decisions.reason: The upper room was built on the flat roof of the house. Readable names God where it adds a pronoun for him.

records.source: אֱ֠דַיִן גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ הַרְגִּ֔שׁוּ וְהַשְׁכַּ֖חוּ לְדָנִיֵּ֑אל בָּעֵ֥א וּמִתְחַנַּ֖ן קֳדָ֥ם אֱלָהֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Then the men these came thronging and found Daniel asking and seeking favor before his God.
pieces: Then these men went as a group and found Daniel praying and asking his God for help.

L.12: Then these men came thronging and found Daniel making petition and pleading before his God.

R.12: Then those men went to Daniel's house together. They found him praying and asking his God to help him.

decisions.choice: asking and seeking favor: making petition, the very act forbidden
decisions.reason: The first verb is the word of the decree, "to ask a petition" (verse 8). Daniel is found doing exactly what the decree forbade.

decisions.choice: came thronging: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: See verse 7.

decisions.choice: went as a group (B); went together (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

records.heading: Daniel in the lions' den

records.source: בֵּ֠אדַיִן קְרִ֨יבוּ וְאָמְרִ֥ין קֳדָם־מַלְכָּא֮ עַל־אֱסָ֣ר מַלְכָּא֒ הֲלָ֧א אֱסָ֣ר רְשַׁ֗מְתָּ דִּ֣י כָל־אֱנָ֡שׁ דִּֽי־יִבְעֵה֩ מִן־כָּל־אֱלָ֨הּ וֶֽאֱנָ֜שׁ עַד־יוֹמִ֣ין תְּלָתִ֗ין לָהֵן֙ מִנָּ֣ךְ מַלְכָּ֔א יִתְרְמֵ֕א לְג֖וֹב אַרְיָותָ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר יַצִּיבָ֧א מִלְּתָ֛א כְּדָת־מָדַ֥י וּפָרַ֖ס דִּי־לָ֥א תֶעְדֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: Then they approached and saying before the king concerning the prohibition of the king: Did you not sign a prohibition that any man who asks from any god or man for thirty days, except from you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions? Answering the king and saying: Certain [is] the matter, according to [the] law of [the] Medes and Persians, which does not pass away.
pieces: So they went to the king and spoke to him about his ban: "O king, did you not sign a ban saying that anyone who prays to any god or human being for thirty days, except to you, would be thrown into the lions' den?" The king answered, "That decree stands, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."

L.13: Then they came near and spoke before the king about the king's prohibition: "Did you not sign a prohibition that any person who makes a petition to any god or man for thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the den of lions?" The king answered, saying, "Certain [is] the matter, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not pass away."

R.13: So they went to the king and reminded him of the law he had made. They said, "Your Majesty, did you not sign a law that for thirty days no one may pray to any god or human being except to you? Did you not say that anyone who disobeys will be thrown into a pit of lions?" The king answered, "Yes, that is the law. The laws of the Medes and the Persians cannot be cancelled."

decisions.choice: did you not sign: the plotters make the king confirm the decree first
decisions.reason: Before naming Daniel, they have the king state that the decree cannot be changed. Only then do they spring the trap (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the law of the Medes and Persians: as in verse 9
decisions.reason: The king repeats the words of verse 9.

decisions.choice: two questions (R)
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long question in two.

records.source: בֵּ֠אדַיִן עֲנ֣וֹ וְאָמְרִין֮ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּא֒ דִּ֣י דָנִיֵּ֡אל דִּי֩ מִן־בְּנֵ֨י גָלוּתָ֜א דִּ֣י יְה֗וּד לָא־שָׂ֨ם עֲלָ֤ךְ מַלְכָּא֙ טְעֵ֔ם וְעַל־אֱסָרָ֖א דִּ֣י רְשַׁ֑מְתָּ וְזִמְנִ֤ין תְּלָתָה֙ בְּיוֹמָ֔א בָּעֵ֖א בָּעוּתֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Then they answered and saying before the king: Daniel, who [is] from the sons of the exile of Judah, not has set on you, O king, regard, nor on the prohibition that you signed; and three times in the day he is asking his petition.
pieces: Then they said to the king, "Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the ban you signed. He still prays three times a day."

L.14: Then they answered and said before the king, "Daniel, who is one of the exiles of Judah, pays no regard to you, O king, or to the prohibition that you signed; but three times a day he makes his petition."

R.14: Then they told the king, "Daniel, one of the captives from Judah, is not paying any attention to you, Your Majesty, or to the law you signed. He still prays to his God three times every day."

decisions.choice: Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah: the accusers stress that he is a foreigner
decisions.reason: They do not call him by his rank; they call him a captive from Judah, as Belshazzar did (5:13), as if to suggest that his loyalty is doubtful.

decisions.choice: pays no regard to you: shows no respect for your authority
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the three friends in 3:12. The accusers turn Daniel's prayer into an insult to the king.

decisions.choice: prays to his God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what Daniel's "petition" was.

records.source: אֱדַ֨יִן מַלְכָּ֜א כְּדִ֧י מִלְּתָ֣א שְׁמַ֗ע שַׂגִּיא֙ בְּאֵ֣שׁ עֲל֔וֹהִי וְעַ֧ל דָּנִיֵּ֛אל שָׂ֥ם בָּ֖ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתֵ֑הּ וְעַד֙ מֶֽעָלֵ֣י שִׁמְשָׁ֔א הֲוָ֥א מִשְׁתַּדַּ֖ר לְהַצָּלוּתֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Then the king, when the word he heard, greatly it displeased him, and concerning Daniel he set [his] mind to deliver him, and until [the] going down of the sun he was striving to rescue him.
pieces: When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed. He was determined to save Daniel, and until sunset he tried everything he could to rescue him.

L.15: Then when the king heard the word, it displeased him greatly; and he set his mind on Daniel, to deliver him, and until the going down of the sun he was striving to rescue him.

R.15: When the king heard this, he was very upset. He wanted to save Daniel. All day long, until the sun went down, he tried to find a way to rescue him.

decisions.choice: greatly it displeased him: he was deeply distressed
decisions.reason: The king is angry, not with Daniel, but with himself or with those who tricked him. Unlike Nebuchadnezzar in chapter 3, Darius wants to save the accused.

decisions.choice: until the going down of the sun: the decree had to be carried out that day
decisions.reason: The king seems to have had until evening to act. He searched for a way around his own law, but found none (verse 16).

decisions.choice: All day long (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "All day long" to show how hard the king tried.

records.source: בֵּאדַ֨יִן֙ גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ עַל־מַלְכָּ֑א וְאָמְרִ֣ין לְמַלְכָּ֗א דַּ֤ע מַלְכָּא֙ דִּֽי־דָת֙ לְמָדַ֣י וּפָרַ֔ס דִּֽי־כָל־אֱסָ֥ר וּקְיָ֛ם דִּֽי־מַלְכָּ֥א יְהָקֵ֖ים לָ֥א לְהַשְׁנָיָֽה׃
records.gloss: Then the men these came thronging to the king and saying to the king: Know, O king, that [the] law of [the] Medes and Persians [is] that any prohibition and statute which the king establishes not [is] to be changed.
pieces: Then these men went as a group to the king and said, "Do not forget, O king, that under the law of the Medes and Persians no ban or decree the king issues can be changed."

L.16: Then these men came thronging to the king, saying to the king, "Know, O king, that [it is] the law of [the] Medes and Persians that any prohibition or statute which the king establishes is not to be changed."

R.16: Then those men went to the king together and said, "Your Majesty, remember that by the laws of the Medes and the Persians, no law that the king makes can be changed."

decisions.choice: know, O king: a reminder with an edge of threat
decisions.reason: The men remind the king that his own law binds him. If he set it aside, his authority would be in doubt.

decisions.choice: came thronging: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: See verse 7.

decisions.choice: Do not forget (B); remember (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "know"; Balanced and Readable say "do not forget" and "remember", since the king already knows the law.

records.source: בֵּאדַ֜יִן מַלְכָּ֣א אֲמַ֗ר וְהַיְתִיו֙ לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל וּרְמ֕וֹ לְגֻבָּ֖א דִּ֣י אַרְיָוָתָ֑א עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֔אל אֱלָהָ֗ךְ דִּ֣י אַ֤נְתְּ פָּֽלַֽח־לֵהּ֙ בִּתְדִירָ֔א ה֖וּא יְשֵׁיזְבִנָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Then the king said, and they brought Daniel and threw [him] into the den of the lions. Answering the king and saying to Daniel: Your God, whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.
pieces: So the king gave the order, and Daniel was brought and thrown into the lions' den. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve faithfully, rescue you!"

L.17: Then the king spoke, and they brought Daniel and threw [him] into the lions' den. The king answered, saying to Daniel, "Your God, whom you are serving continually, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will deliver you!"

R.17: So the king gave the order. Daniel was brought and thrown into the pit of lions. The king said to Daniel, "You have always been faithful to your God. I hope that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save you!"

decisions.choice: your God ... will deliver you: a hope or a wish
decisions.reason: The verb form can state what will happen ("he will deliver you") or express a wish ("may he deliver you"). The king can do nothing more; he hopes that Daniel's God can. In verse 21 he asks whether God was able.

decisions.choice: whom you serve continually: Daniel's faithful worship
decisions.reason: "Serve" is the word for religious service to God (3:12, 17). "Continually" recalls Daniel's daily prayer (verse 11).

decisions.choice: he will deliver (L); May ... rescue (B); I hope that he will save (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the open form; Balanced and Readable take the sense of a wish (m1). The pronoun for Daniel's God takes the divine pronoun setting, though the king speaks, as with Nebuchadnezzar in 3:28.

records.source: וְהֵיתָ֨יִת֙ אֶ֣בֶן חֲדָ֔ה וְשֻׂמַ֖ת עַל־פֻּ֣ם גֻּבָּ֑א וְחַתְמַ֨הּ מַלְכָּ֜א בְּעִזְקְתֵ֗הּ וּבְעִזְקָת֙ רַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי דִּ֛י לָא־תִשְׁנֵ֥א צְב֖וּ בְּדָנִיֵּֽאל׃
records.gloss: And was brought a stone one and was placed on [the] mouth of the den, and sealed it the king with his signet ring and with [the] signet rings of his nobles, that not would be changed [the] purpose concerning Daniel.
pieces: Then a stone was brought and set over the opening of the den. The king sealed it with his own ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that Daniel's sentence could not be changed.

L.18: And a stone, one, was brought and placed on the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it up with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.

R.18: A large stone was brought and put over the opening of the pit. The king put his seal on it with his own ring and with the rings of his officials. That way no one could change what had been done to Daniel.

decisions.choice: sealed it with his signet ring: a sign that no one could open it
decisions.reason: A seal of clay or wax was pressed with the king's ring across the stone; if anyone moved the stone, the broken seal would show it. The nobles' seals guard against the king himself secretly freeing Daniel (compare Matthew 27:66).

decisions.choice: so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel
decisions.reason: The word may mean "purpose" or "matter": the sentence on Daniel could not be changed, whether to rescue him or to harm him further.

decisions.choice: put his seal on it (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the seal in plain words (m1).

records.source: אֱ֠דַיִן אֲזַ֨ל מַלְכָּ֤א לְהֵֽיכְלֵהּ֙ וּבָ֣ת טְוָ֔ת וְדַחֲוָ֖ן לָא־הַנְעֵ֣ל קָֽדָמ֑וֹהִי וְשִׁנְתֵּ֖הּ נַדַּ֥ת עֲלֽוֹהִי׃
records.gloss: Then went the king to his palace and passed the night fasting, and diversions not were brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.
pieces: Then the king went back to his palace and spent the night without eating. He allowed no entertainment to be brought to him, and he could not sleep.

L.19: Then the king went off to his palace and passed the night fasting; and no diversions were brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.

R.19: Then the king went back to his palace. He did not eat anything all night. He did not want anyone to entertain him. And he could not sleep.

decisions.choice: diversions: entertainment, of a kind not certain
decisions.reason: The word is used only here and its meaning is not known. It may mean entertainment, musicians, food, or women of the harem. Whatever it was, the king refused it.

decisions.choice: his sleep fled from him: he could not sleep
decisions.reason: Compare 2:1, where Nebuchadnezzar's dreams kept him awake.

decisions.choice: entertainment (B); entertain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the most general sense of the uncertain word (m1).

records.source: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֔א בִּשְׁפַּרְפָּרָ֖א יְק֣וּם בְּנָגְהָ֑א וּבְהִ֨תְבְּהָלָ֔ה לְגֻבָּ֥א דִֽי־אַרְיָוָתָ֖א אֲזַֽל׃
records.gloss: Then the king at dawn rose up at daylight, and in haste to the den of the lions he went.
pieces: At daybreak, as soon as it was light, the king rose and went in haste to the lions' den.

L.20: Then the king rose at dawn, at first light, and went in haste to the den of lions.

R.20: As soon as the sun began to rise, the king got up and hurried to the pit of lions.

decisions.choice: at dawn, at first light: as early as possible
decisions.reason: Two words for the dawn stand together: the king rose at the very first light.

decisions.choice: At daybreak, as soon as it was light (B); As soon as the sun began to rise (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two words for dawn.

records.source: וּכְמִקְרְבֵ֣הּ לְגֻבָּ֔א לְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל בְּקָ֥ל עֲצִ֖יב זְעִ֑ק עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֗אל דָּֽנִיֵּאל֙ עֲבֵד֙ אֱלָהָ֣א חַיָּ֔א אֱלָהָ֗ךְ דִּ֣י אַ֤נְתְּ פָּֽלַֽח־לֵהּ֙ בִּתְדִירָ֔א הַיְכִ֥ל לְשֵׁיזָבוּתָ֖ךְ מִן־אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃
records.gloss: And when he came near to the den to Daniel, with a voice anguished he cried out; answering the king and saying to Daniel: Daniel, servant of the living God, your God whom you serve continually, was he able to deliver you from the lions?
pieces: When he came near the den, he called out to Daniel in an anguished voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God! Has your God, whom you faithfully serve, been able to rescue you from the lions?"

L.21: And when he came near the den, he cried out to Daniel with an anguished voice. The king answered and said to Daniel, "Daniel, servant of the living God, your God, whom you are serving continually, was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} able to deliver you from the lions?"

R.21: When he came near the pit, he called out to Daniel in a worried voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God! You have always been faithful to your God. Has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} been able to save you from the lions?"

decisions.choice: the living God: the God who is alive and acts
decisions.reason: The title sets Israel's God against idols that cannot see or hear or act (5:23; Jeremiah 10:10). Darius uses it again in his decree (verse 27).

decisions.choice: with an anguished voice: in distress
decisions.reason: The word means pained or grieved. The king fears the worst.

decisions.choice: able to deliver (L); able to rescue (B); able to save (R)
decisions.reason: The words take up the king's hope of verse 17. Readable splits the long question and adds a pronoun for God, which takes the divine pronoun setting.

records.source: אֱדַ֨יִן֙ דָּנִיֶּ֔אל עִם־מַלְכָּ֖א מַלִּ֑ל מַלְכָּ֖א לְעָלְמִ֥ין חֱיִֽי׃
records.gloss: Then Daniel with the king spoke: O king, forever live!
pieces: Then Daniel answered the king, "O king, may you live forever!

L.22: Then Daniel spoke with the king: "O king, live forever!

R.22: Daniel answered, "Your Majesty, may you live forever!

decisions.choice: O king, live forever: Daniel answers with the court's greeting
decisions.reason: Daniel greets the king with the usual courtesy (2:4). He bears no grudge against the king.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:4.

records.source: אֱלָהִ֞י שְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאֲכֵ֗הּ וּֽסֲגַ֛ר פֻּ֥ם אַרְיָוָתָ֖א וְלָ֣א חַבְּל֑וּנִי כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֤י קָֽדָמ֨וֹהִי֙ זָכוּ֙ הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת לִ֔י וְאַ֤ף קָֽדָמָךְ֙ מַלְכָּ֔א חֲבוּלָ֖ה לָ֥א עַבְדֵֽת׃
records.gloss: My God sent his angel and shut the mouth of the lions, and they have not harmed me, because that before him innocence was found in me; and also before you, O king, a crime I have not done.
pieces: My God sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel and shut the lions' mouths, and they have not hurt me, because I was found innocent in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sight. And I have done nothing wrong before you either, O king."

L.23: My God has sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel and has shut the mouth of the lions, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and also before you, O king, I have done no wrong."

R.23: My God sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angel to shut the lions' mouths. They have not hurt me, because God knows that I have done nothing wrong. And I have never done anything wrong to you, Your Majesty."

decisions.choice: God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths
decisions.reason: As with the three friends (3:28), God sends his angel to rescue his servant. Hebrews 11:33 speaks of those who by faith "shut the mouths of lions".

decisions.choice: innocent before God, and no wrong before the king
decisions.reason: Daniel's obedience to God was no crime against the king. He did not disobey to harm the king, but because a higher law bound him.

decisions.choice: God knows that I have done nothing wrong (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "innocence was found before him" means.

records.source: בֵּאדַ֣יִן מַלְכָּ֗א שַׂגִּיא֙ טְאֵ֣ב עֲל֔וֹהִי וּלְדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל אֲמַ֖ר לְהַנְסָקָ֣ה מִן־גֻּבָּ֑א וְהֻסַּ֨ק דָּנִיֵּ֜אל מִן־גֻּבָּ֗א וְכָל־חֲבָל֙ לָא־הִשְׁתְּכַ֣ח בֵּ֔הּ דִּ֖י הֵימִ֥ן בֵּאלָהֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Then the king greatly it was good to him, and Daniel he said to take up from the den; and Daniel was taken up from the den, and any hurt not was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
pieces: The king was overjoyed and ordered that Daniel be lifted out of the den. So Daniel was lifted out, and no injury of any kind was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

L.24: Then the king was exceedingly glad, and Daniel he ordered to be taken up out of the den. And Daniel was lifted out of the den, and no hurt at all was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

R.24: The king was very happy. He ordered his servants to lift Daniel out of the pit. So they lifted him out, and he had no wounds at all, because he had trusted in his God.

decisions.choice: because he had trusted in his God: faith was the reason
decisions.reason: The narrator gives the reason for Daniel's rescue: his trust in God. The verb is from the same root as "trustworthy" in verse 5.

decisions.choice: no harm was found on him: as with the three in the fire
decisions.reason: Compare 3:27, where the fire had no power over the bodies of the three.

decisions.choice: his servants (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names who lifted Daniel out.

records.source: וַאֲמַ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א וְהַיְתִ֞יו גֻּבְרַיָּ֤א אִלֵּךְ֙ דִּֽי־אֲכַ֤לוּ קַרְצ֨וֹהִי֙ דִּ֣י דָֽנִיֵּ֔אל וּלְגֹ֤ב אַרְיָוָתָא֙ רְמ֔וֹ אִנּ֖וּן בְּנֵיה֣וֹן וּנְשֵׁיה֑וֹן וְלָֽא־מְט֞וֹ לְאַרְעִ֣ית גֻּבָּ֗א עַ֠ד דִּֽי־שְׁלִ֤טֽוּ בְהוֹן֙ אַרְיָ֣וָתָ֔א וְכָל־גַּרְמֵיה֖וֹן הַדִּֽקוּ׃
records.gloss: And said the king, and they brought the men these who had eaten the pieces of Daniel, and into the den of the lions they threw them, their sons and their wives; and not had they reached the bottom of the den until the lions overpowered them, and all their bones they crushed.
pieces: Then at the king's command the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions' den, together with their children and their wives. They had not yet reached the floor of the den when the lions overpowered them and broke all their bones.

L.25: And the king gave the order, and they brought those men who had eaten the pieces of Daniel, and into the den of lions they threw them, them, their {{gender:children|sons}} and their wives; and they had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.

R.25: Then the king gave another order. The men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought to the pit. They were thrown into the pit of lions, and their wives and children with them. Before they reached the bottom of the pit, the lions attacked them and crushed all their bones.

decisions.choice: who had eaten the pieces of Daniel: who had maliciously accused him
decisions.reason: The same idiom as in 3:8.

decisions.choice: their children and their wives: punishment of the whole family
decisions.reason: Punishing a guilty man's family with him was a practice of ancient empires; the Greek historian Herodotus records it of the Persians, and Esther 9:13-14 tells of Haman's sons. The law of Moses forbade putting children to death for their parents' sins (Deuteronomy 24:16; 2 Kings 14:6). The text reports the king's act without approving it.

decisions.choice: before they reached the bottom: the lions were not tame
decisions.reason: The detail answers any claim that the lions were not hungry: God, not chance, had kept Daniel safe.

decisions.choice: the punishment stated plainly
decisions.reason: Each level states the punishment as the text does, without softening or adding to it. Literal keeps the idiom "eaten the pieces", as in 3:8; Balanced and Readable give its sense (m1). "Sons" here means children, sons and daughters, so Literal gives it with the gender setting and Balanced and Readable say "children".

records.source: בֵּאדַ֜יִן דָּרְיָ֣וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א כְּ֠תַב לְֽכָל־עַֽמְמַיָּ֞א אֻמַיָּ֧א וְלִשָּׁנַיָּ֛א דִּֽי־דָיְרִ֥ין בְּכָל־אַרְעָ֖א שְׁלָמְכ֥וֹן יִשְׂגֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: Then Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages who dwell in all the earth: Your peace may it increase!
pieces: Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations and people of every language who live in all the earth: "May you have abundant peace!

L.26: Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages that are dwelling in all the earth: "May your peace increase!

R.26: Then King Darius wrote this letter to people of every nation and language all over the world: "I wish you peace and success!

decisions.choice: the greeting of Nebuchadnezzar's letter
decisions.reason: Darius writes in the same words as Nebuchadnezzar in 3:31. The two kings, Babylonian and Mede, end by praising the God of Daniel.

decisions.choice: the wording of 3:31; a quotation mark
decisions.reason: Each level reuses its wording of 3:31. Here, unlike Nebuchadnezzar's letter, the narrator quotes the decree, so it opens a quotation. The greeting is one unit in the Aramaic accents and stays on one line.

records.source: מִן־קֳדָמַי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּ֣י׀בְּכָל־שָׁלְטָ֣ן מַלְכוּתִ֗י לֶהֱוֺ֤ן זָיְעִין֙ וְדָ֣חֲלִ֔ין מִן־קֳדָ֖ם אֱלָהֵ֣הּ דִּי־דָֽנִיֵּ֑אל דִּי־ה֣וּא׀אֱלָהָ֣א חַיָּ֗א וְקַיָּם֙ לְעָ֣לְמִ֔ין וּמַלְכוּתֵהּ֙ דִּֽי־לָ֣א תִתְחַבַּ֔ל וְשָׁלְטָנֵ֖הּ עַד־סוֹפָֽא׃
records.gloss: From before me is made a decree, that in all [the] dominion of my kingdom they will be trembling and fearing before [the] God of Daniel; for he [is] the God living and enduring forever, and his kingdom [is one] which will not be destroyed, and his dominion [is] to the end.
pieces: I decree that in every part of my kingdom \q people must tremble with fear \q before the God of Daniel, \q because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the living God, who endures forever; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom will never be destroyed, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rule will never end.

L.27: From me a decree is made, \q that in all the dominion of my kingdom [people] are to be trembling and fearing \q before the God of Daniel; \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, the living God, is enduring forever; \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom [is one] that will not be destroyed, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dominion [will be] to the end.

R.27: I order everyone in my kingdom \q to fear and respect the God of Daniel. \q He is the living God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will live forever. \q His kingdom will never be destroyed. \q His rule will never end.

decisions.choice: his kingdom will not be destroyed, and his dominion is to the end: as 2:44 and 4:31
decisions.reason: Darius's words take up the hope of 2:44 ("a kingdom that will never be destroyed") and the praise of 3:33 and 4:31. The same words are used of the kingdom of the one like a son of man (7:14).

decisions.choice: tremble and fear: stand in reverent awe
decisions.reason: These were the words used of the peoples' fear of Nebuchadnezzar (5:19). Now they are turned toward God. Darius does not command the worship of Daniel's God only, but reverence for him.

decisions.choice: set in lines at the Aramaic accents
decisions.reason: The terms for Daniel set 6:27-28 in lines. Readable merges two short lines of the first half.

records.source: מְשֵׁיזִ֣ב וּמַצִּ֗ל וְעָבֵד֙ אָתִ֣ין וְתִמְהִ֔ין בִּשְׁמַיָּ֖א וּבְאַרְעָ֑א דִּ֚י שֵׁיזִ֣יב לְדָֽנִיֵּ֔אל מִן־יַ֖ד אַרְיָוָתָֽא׃
records.gloss: Delivering and rescuing and doing signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth, who has delivered Daniel from [the] hand of the lions.
pieces: He saves and rescues; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does signs and wonders \q in heaven and on earth. \q He has rescued Daniel \q from the power of the lions."

L.28: He delivers and rescues, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} works signs and wonders \q in the heavens and on the earth, \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who has delivered Daniel \q from the power of the lions."

R.28: He saves and rescues people. \q He does amazing things in heaven and on earth. \q He has saved Daniel from the lions."

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: as in 3:32
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar's letter spoke of the signs and wonders God had done for him (3:32-33). Darius now says the same of what God did for Daniel.

decisions.choice: the hand of the lions: the power of the lions
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, even of animals (1 Samuel 17:37, "the paw of the lion").

decisions.choice: He (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The verse begins with verbs and no subject in the Aramaic, continuing the description of God in verse 27. Every level starts a new sentence with "He", which Literal does not bracket because the Aramaic verb forms carry the subject. The verse is set in lines at the Aramaic accents (Readable in three), and the decree's quotation closes here.

records.source: וְדָנִיֵּ֣אל דְּנָ֔ה הַצְלַ֖ח בְּמַלְכ֣וּת דָּרְיָ֑וֶשׁ וּבְמַלְכ֖וּת כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ פָּרְסָאָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And Daniel this prospered in [the] reign of Darius and in [the] reign of Cyrus the Persian.
pieces: So Daniel prospered during the reigns of Darius and of Cyrus the Persian.

L.29: And this Daniel prospered in the kingship of Darius and in the kingship of Cyrus the Persian.

R.29: So Daniel did well while Darius was king and while Cyrus the Persian was king.

decisions.choice: in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus: two reigns, or one
alternatives: in the reign of Darius, that is, the reign of Cyrus the Persian
decisions.reason: The usual reading is that Daniel prospered under two kings, one after the other. The small word "and" can also mean "that is", and some who identify Darius the Mede with Cyrus (see verse 1) read: "in the reign of Darius, that is, the reign of Cyrus the Persian".

decisions.choice: prospered ... Cyrus: as 1:21 said
decisions.reason: The story of the book's first half closes as chapter 1 did (1:21), with Daniel serving into the reign of Cyrus, the king who let the exiles go home (Ezra 1:1-4).

decisions.choice: did well (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "did well" for "prospered".
